{{Short description|Canadian theoretical physicist, author of books on Black Hole physics}}

[[File:Valeri Frolov 2019.jpg|thumb|Valeri Frolov]]

'''Valeri Frolov''' (born October 7, 1946) is a Russian-born Canadian theoretical [[physicist]] at the [[University of Alberta]], Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Frolov |first=Valeri |title=Veleri Frolov - University of Alberta |url=https://apps.ualberta.ca/directory/person/vfrolov |website=University of Alberta, Department of Physics, Faculty}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Frolov |first=Valeri |title=Killam Memorial Chair |url=https://www.ualberta.ca/graduate-studies/awards-and-funding/killam-laureates/killam-memorial-chairs.html |website=Killam Memorial Chairs}}</ref> His research is concerned with [[black hole]] physics and [[quantum gravity]].

== Background and Education ==
Valeri Frolov was born and grew up in Moscow. He graduated from the [[Moscow State University]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Moscow State University |url=https://msu.ru/en/ |website=Lomonosov Moscow State University}}</ref> and obtained his Master's Degree in 1970. Later, he received his [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree in 1973 and his [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree in 1980, both in theoretical physics from [[Lebedev Physical Institute|P.N. Lebedev Physical Institute]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=P.N. Lebedev Physical Institute |url=http://www.lebedev.ru/ru/main |website=ФИАН}}</ref> Moscow.

== Work ==
Frolov's professional scientific career began in 1970, when he jointed the [[Lebedev Physical Institute|P.N. Lebedev Physical Institute]]. He worked there as an assistant professor, an associate professor, and, from 1980 to 1992, as a full professor. Concurrently, he was also a professor from 1985 to 1992 at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology |url=https://mipt.ru/ |website=MIPT}}</ref> In 1992 he spent one year as a visiting professor at the [[University of Copenhagen]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=University of Copenhagen |url=https://www.ku.dk/english |website=University of Copenhagen|date=29 June 2016 }}</ref> In 1993 he moved to Edmonton, Canada, where he became a full professor at the University of Alberta and received the Killam Memorial Chair, a position which he holds today.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Killam Memorial Chairs {{!}} Faculty of Graduate & Postdoctoral Studies |url=https://www.ualberta.ca/graduate-studies/fees-funding/scholarships-awards/killam-laureates/memorial-chairs.html |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=www.ualberta.ca}}</ref>

== Research ==
Early in his career, Frolov studied [[white hole]]s and semi-closed worlds.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Zel'dovich |first1=Ya. B. |title=Stars and Relativity |last2=Novikov |first2=I. D. |publisher=Dover Publications |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-486-69424-5 |series=Dover Books on Physics}}</ref> In 1970, he and his supervisor, [[Moisey Markov|M.A. Markov]], published a paper which discussed quantum particle creation by charged black holes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Markov |first1=M. A. |last2=Frolov |first2=V. P. |year=1970 |title=Metric of a closed Friedman world perturbed by an electric charge. Theory of electromagnetic 'Friedmons' |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=tmf&paperid=4087&option_lang=eng |journal=Theoretical and Mathematical Physics |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=3–17}}</ref> In 1980, he and Gregory Vilkovisky proposed a model of a regular evaporating black hole and presented a conformal diagram of its spacetime.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Frolov |first1=V. P. |last2=Vilkovisky |first2=G. A. |year=1981 |title=Spherically symmetric collapse in quantum gravity |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370269381905426 |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=106 |issue=4 |pages=307–313|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(81)90542-6 |bibcode=1981PhLB..106..307F |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Later, his main interest focused on quantum effects in black holes. In 1987, he and [[Vitaly Ginzburg]] published a paper on the [[equivalence principle]] in the quantum domain.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ginzburg |first1=V. L. |last2=Frolov |first2=V. P. |year=1987 |title=Vacuum in a homogeneous gravitational field and excitation of a uniformly accelerated detector |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/PU1987v030n12ABEH003071 |journal=Soviet Physics Uspekhi |volume=30 |issue=12 |pages=1073–1095|doi=10.1070/PU1987v030n12ABEH003071 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 1989, he published with [[Kip Thorne]] a paper discussing quantum effects near the horizon of a rotating black hole and proposed a state of the vacuum, which is sometimes referred to as the Frolov-Thorne vacuum.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Frolov |first1=V. P. |last2=Thorne |first2=Kip S. |year=1989 |title=Renormalized stress-energy tensor near the horizon of a slowly evolving, rotating black hole |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.39.2125 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=39 |issue=8 |page=2125|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.39.2125 |pmid=9959893 |bibcode=1989PhRvD..39.2125F |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Black Holes: The Membrane Paradigm |publisher=Yale University Press |year=1986 |isbn=0-300-03770-8 |editor-last=Thorne |editor-first=Kip S. |location=New Haven, CT |editor-last2=Price |editor-first2=Richard H. |editor-last3=Macdonald |editor-first3=Douglas A.}}</ref> In 1994 he (with A. Barvinsky and A. Zelnikov) introduced a no-boundary wave function of a black hole,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Barvinsky |first1=A. O. |last2=Frolov |first2=V. P. |last3=Zelnikov |first3=A. I. |year=1995 |title=Wavefunction of a Black Hole and the Dynamical Origin of Entropy |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.51.1741 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=51 |issue=4 |pages=1741–1763|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.51.1741 |pmid=10018642 |arxiv=gr-qc/9404036 |bibcode=1995PhRvD..51.1741B }}</ref> and in 1996 he with (D. Fursaev and A. Zelnikov) proposed an explanation of the black hole entropy based on [[Andrei Sakharov|Sakharov]]'s ideas of [[induced gravity]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Visser |first=Matt |year=2002 |title=Sakharov's induced gravity: a modern perspective |journal=Modern Physics Letters A |volume=17 |issue=15n17 |pages=977–991|doi=10.1142/S0217732302006886 |arxiv=gr-qc/0204062 }}</ref> During the same period of time, he also studied [[cosmic string]]s,<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Vilenkin |first1=A. |title=Cosmic Strings and Other Topological Defects |last2=Shellard |first2=E. P. S. |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2000 |isbn=978-0-521-65476-0 |series=Cambridge Monographs on Mathematical Physics}}</ref> their interaction with black holes, and quantum effects in the string background; wormholes and "time machines;"<ref>{{Cite book |last=Visser |first=Matt |title=Lorentzian wormholes: from Einstein to Hawking |publisher=American Institute of Physics |year=1996 |isbn=978-1-56396-653-8 |location=Woodbury, N.Y.}}</ref> and regular black hole models. From 2006 to 2018 the main focus of his research was on the hidden symmetries of black holes of dimension four and higher.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Frolov |first1=Valeri P. |last2=Kubizňák |first2=David |date=5 January 2007 |title=Hidden Symmetries of Higher-Dimensional Rotating Black Holes |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.011101 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=98 |issue=1 |article-number=011101|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.011101 |pmid=17358466 |arxiv=gr-qc/0605058 |bibcode=2007PhRvL..98a1101F }}</ref> In collaboration with D. Kubizňák and P. Krtouš, he demonstrated that all these solutions of the Einstein equations possessed a special geometrical object, called the [[Wilhelm Killing|Killing]]-[[Kentaro Yano (mathematician)|Yano]] tensor, which is responsible for a complete integrability of the equations of motion of particles and a separability of most interesting physical field equations in these spacetimes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Frolov |first1=V.P. |last2=Krtouš |first2=P. |last3=Kubizňák |first3=D. |date=22 November 2017 |title=Black holes, hidden symmetries, and complete integrability |journal=Living Reviews in Relativity |volume=20 |issue=6 |page=6 |doi=10.1007/s41114-017-0009-9 |pmid=29213211 |pmc=5700430 |arxiv=1705.05482|bibcode=2017LRR....20....6F }}</ref> More recently, he proposed an effective action for electromagnetic and gravitational spin-optics, which is a generalization of the standard geometric optics and which takes into account the interaction of the spin of these fields with the spacetime curvature.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Frolov |first=Valeri P. |date=6 October 2020 |title=Maxwell equations in a curved spacetime: Spin optics approximation |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.102.084013 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=102 |issue=8 |article-number=084013 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.102.084013 |arxiv=2007.03743 |bibcode=2020PhRvD.102h4013F |via=APS}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* Killam Memorial Chair (1993 to present)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Frolov |first=Valeri |title=Killam Memorial Chair |url=https://www.ualberta.ca/graduate-studies/awards-and-funding/killam-laureates/killam-memorial-chairs.html |website=Killam Memorial Chairs}}</ref>
* Markov Prize<ref>{{Cite web |last=Frolov |first=Valeri |title=Markov Prize |url=https://www.inr.ac.ru/a/i/6441e.htm}}</ref> of the [[Institute for Nuclear Research]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute for Nuclear Research |url=http://inr.ru/english.html |website=Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> for outstanding contributions to black hole theory (2016)
